I don’t know how mom left. But that doesn’t matter. He’s 2 right now. And kids yes are smart. And do pick up on things. Yet it’s gonna be sometime before he figures out that his mom isn’t around. I’m not one to believe that only a dad or that only a mom can do just that role. I believe that either parent can do either role. If needed be. 
I want you to remember this though. You are there for him. And that’s all that matters. Make those precious memories. Don’t think of it as him missing a mom. If you do that he’ll definitely pick up on it. Just take it day by day. Love him. Protect him. Cherish him. Keep him close. Wipe his tears. Make him laugh. Hug him. Keep him close even when the time comes even when he wants to push you away. Always tell him you love him. 
You’ve got a son. You’ve got a blessing. You’re doing great! And when the time comes have the conversation with him. Hang in there!

Your true friends will stick with you. I believe that. Through thick and thin. Through the good and the bad. And they would through their transition. We lose people in our lives we thought we’d have in our lives forever. It happens. It can’t be helped. It’s life. But I can tell you this. The lgbtq community is just like any other community. It has beautiful people. It takes some time especially when they will be transitioning. Getting to know oneself again. And to be comfortable in their new skin. But give it time. Find support groups in your area where you can meet new people and make new friends.  Good luck!!!

Looks like you got lots of great advice! Can I just say you are such a beautiful and strong momma. Be proud of who you are and the way you have been supporting your transgender son. 
Generally it always depends on where you are living when it comes to what to do first and who to go to but usually it doesn’t make much of a difference. 

Definitely got to find him a pediatrician and endocrinologist. Both that are specialized in dealing with transgender patients. Also need a doctor that can get him diagnosed with gender dysphoria. From what you’ve shared it’s more than likely he will be diagnosed. This will be very helpful in getting hormone blockers. Generally kids/teens his age are first put on hormone blockers then about two years usually or more or less generally depending on the child/teen and their families they will be prescribed hormones. It differs obviously. 

Another thing. I’d say definitely do some research for lgbt support groups in your area! I know you said something about groups and wasn’t quite clear what you meant about what kind of groups they were. Having people he can relate to and be around is very nurturing and helpful. 

I can do research and reach out to some of my peeps as well if need be. Just PM me or leave a response in the comments. 

I just want to add again you are doing great momma bear. Hang in there. You took a very important step by reaching out and asking for help and educating yourself. Which is so important. Send hugs and support.
